title: TrailGenic Eccentric Load Stress Inversion Dataset
description: Shell dataset module modeling eccentric muscular stress and adaptation during downhill endurance activity.

records.mechanism: Repeated downhill eccentric load is absorbed without accumulated autonomic strain after the recovery inflection

stimulus.terrain_context: technical alpine descents and large elevation-loss sessions

physiological_response: Eccentric descent load no longer predicts persistent Day-2 autonomic suppression after the inflection.
Technical terrain may slow movement enough to preserve deeper aerobic output while still imposing muscular load.
Day-2 restoration across Hikes 16-22 suggests muscular stress was absorbed rather than accumulated.
adaptation_outcomes: Improved downhill resilience across repeated mountain exposure.
Lower risk that eccentric muscular stress becomes systemic overreaching when recovery architecture is intact.
Supports progression toward higher-load alpine routes with sleep-gated Day-1 monitoring.

supporting_science.finding: Repeated eccentric exposure can produce protective adaptations that reduce subsequent muscle damage.

records.mechanism: Eccentric muscle loading during downhill movement
adaptation_outcomes: reduced muscle damage in repeated exposure

supporting_science.finding: Eccentric contractions cause muscle damage but stimulate protective adaptations with repeated exposure.
